mathematical_ledger.claim: The interval kernel encloses supplied finite double trajectory parameters using outward long-double operations and a Taylor remainder.
conditions: The caller-supplied trajectory is the intended model
mathematical_ledger.does_not_prove: Correct game trajectory construction, semantic radii, raster definition or original-game floating-point behavior

mathematical_ledger.claim: Pixel mapping and ideal 60-degree hex rotation do not commute when y scale is 71 rather than 82*sqrt(3)/2.

kernel_review.soundness_scope: Supplied double trajectory parameters, not caller construction or original-game mapping
positive_controls: Outward nextafter around primitive long-double operations
Taylor remainder for sin/cos with absolute angle at most 8
Uncertain on invalid input, fast-math or exhausted subdivision
kernel_review.subdivision_enclosure: Rounded midpoint reach uses upward-rounded max(mid-low,high-mid); degenerate midpoints return Uncertain before interval-wide separation. Runtime certification requires nearest rounding and rejects x86 DAZ/FTZ. This does not close caller/game mapping obligations.

continuous_enclosure.scope: Ideal real trajectory defined by supplied double parameters over a closed subinterval of [0,1]; not reference float interpolation, integer snapping or original-game motion
continuous_enclosure.algorithm: Enclose the rounded midpoint position with outward interval arithmetic; expand each coordinate by upward-rounded SpeedBound times max of upward-rounded distances from the computed midpoint to both endpoints. The computed midpoint need only lie inside the interval.
continuous_enclosure.environment: IEEE nearest-rounded basic operations with gradual underflow and per-operation compiler semantics; reject non-nearest rounding, x86 DAZ/FTZ and __FAST_MATH__. This is not certification of arbitrary compiler flags or non-x86 floating-point controls.
continuous_enclosure.limitations: No reference/game error envelope or dynamic certification caller; regression tests do not replace an arithmetic or game-mapping proof.
